name: Al-Hallaj
contribution: A Muslim Iranian mystic, poet, preacher, and teacher of Sufism, and one of the most controversial figures in Islamic history.
legacy: His most famous utterance, anā this person, was interpreted by many as a claim to divinity, while others understood it as an expression of the annihilation of the individual ego in which God, rather than the individual self, speaks through the mystic

checks.lead: Mansour al-Hallaj (Arabic: ابو المغيث الحسين بن منصور الحلاج, romanized: Abū 'l-Muġīth al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr al-Ḥallāj), also known as Mansour Hallaj (Persian: منصور حلاج, romanized: Mansūr-e Hallāj; c. 858 – 26 March 922; c. 244 AH – 309 AH), was a Muslim Iranian mystic, poet, preacher, and teacher of Sufism, and one of the most controversial figures in Islamic history. During his lifetime he attracted a large popular following and was acclaimed as a saint by many ordinary believers, while Muslim jurists condemned him as a heretic. Most of his contemporary Sufis likewise disapproved of his actions, although he later became a major figure in the Sufi tradition.
